questions.question_text: Marine biologist Ayesha Rahman spent three seasons recording the clicks of sperm whales off the coast of Dominica. She noticed that whales in the same family group repeated a short pattern of clicks, called a coda, far more often than whales from other groups did. Rahman argues that these shared codas work much like a family name: they let a whale signal which group it belongs to.
questions.question_prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

A.text: Rahman found that sperm whales can only communicate with members of their own family group.

B.text: Rahman's recordings suggest that sperm whales use shared click patterns to identify their group.

C.text: Rahman discovered that codas are learned from whales in other family groups.

D.text: Rahman concluded that sperm whales stop producing codas once they leave the coast of Dominica.

questions.question_text: Many cities plant trees along streets to cool neighborhoods in summer. A 2024 survey of twelve cities, however, found that newly planted trees lowered street temperatures only after their canopies had grown for at least eight years. Planners who expect quick results may therefore be disappointed, even though the long-term benefits are well documented.
questions.question_prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

A.text: It introduces a finding that qualifies the expectation described in the first sentence.

B.text: It provides an example of a city that stopped planting trees.

C.text: It explains why the long-term benefits of trees are well documented.

D.text: It describes a method planners use to choose which trees to plant.
